=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:106 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The live copy still describes the pre-#5082 evidence rule ("unless this turn posted the `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` comment (at most twice per session)") while the workflow-templates twin at line 106 correctly describes the verified-comment-plus-label evidence ("unless this turn posted a verified blocker on the source issue: the `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` comment, whose result carries its URL, and the `ai:claude-blocked` label on that same issue (issue #5082; the accepted forms are in CLAUDE.md §28.G)").
  WHY: Sessions reading the Issue Mode instructions from the live `.claude/` copy would see outdated rules that do not mention the label requirement or the result-URL verification. They would learn only to post the comment, missing the requirement to also add the ai:claude-blocked label and have the result carry the comment URL. The twin-first workflow means the twin is already correct and this is a staged fix pending the Q40 sync; test_template_parity[commands/implement-plan-claude.md] will fail in CI until synced.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:332-333 (_and_chain_segments, the `elif char == "\\"` branch) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The backslash escape handling treats `\` as an escape character in all quoting contexts, but in POSIX shell, single-quoted strings (`'...'`) treat backslash literally; `\` inside single quotes is not an escape. The function at line 329-331 checks `state == "'"` only for `char == "'"`, then falls through to the universal `char == "\\"` branch at 332 which unconditionally skips the next character.
  WHY: A `gh api` command with a backslash preceding a syntax character inside single quotes (e.g. `-f body='hello\;world'`) is valid shell — the `\;` inside single quotes is literal data. The hook's `_and_chain_segments` would see the `;` as a command separator after the backslash skip and incorrectly classify the entire command as holding prohibited syntax, causing the `gh api` parser to reject it. The practical impact is limited to blocker comments whose body contains backslash-followed-by-syntax-character sequences inside single-quoted arguments. The STOP_BLOCK_CAP of 2 provides a safety net.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
